newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian shilling falls, more losses expected.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian shilling falls, more losses expected.

text.p: The Tanzanian shilling ended the week lower against the dollar for the fifth consecutive day and also fell against the pound, the central bank said.

The shilling dealt at a commercial mean rate of 596.9797 versus Thursday's mean of 596.9700. Against pound, the shilling exchanged at 1,013.3764 compared to 1,010.6732 on Thursday. On Monday, the shilling dealt against the dollar for 596.4453.

But dealers said they were unconcerned at the depreciation, which they described as slight. "This week it's (shilling) depreciating four to five cents every day, which is minimal given the type of market we have here," said a dealer from a major foreign bank.
Another financial analyst said he expected the shilling to continue depreciating at a modest rate in the near term.
"We have two forces working in opposite directions. The budget will continue to improve, and that will tend to make the shilling stronger," the analyst said.

"However, following the holiday lull, I expect economic activity, including import demand, to pick up. And that will increase demand for shillings. My guess is the latter will offset the former and in the near term, we can expect to see a furthur modest depreciation of the shilling," he added.
